title: catpart-export output, schema v1
description: Version-1 summary emitted by `catpart-export <file>` on success (ticket #32), alongside the binary little-endian PLY it writes. The summary describes the decoded CATStdCont nested-store geometry (docs/evidence/2026-11-09-nested-store.md G1, 2026-11-09-vertex-pool.md G2, 2026-11-09-facet-semantics.md G3): the vertex pool in walk order, the triangles decoded under G3's pinned primitive semantics (0x4a/0x42 triangle strips with the alternating flip and phase reset per loop, 0x4c closed polygons fan-triangulated from the first corner, lexicographic-rank references, CCW winding preserved as decoded). Failure is not a summary: classified errors exit nonzero with an error_class JSON line on stderr (missing-geometry-store / undecoded-variant / malformed-*). Evolution is additive within a schema version: consumers must ignore properties they do not know.

schema_version.description: Version of this schema. Bumped only by a breaking output change; additive changes keep the version.

vertex_count.description: Number of PLY vertices: the decoded pool (all 01 06 pool groups flattened in body order, G2 P1g/P2g; 15-byte records [05 08 01][f32le xyz]).

triangle_count.description: Number of PLY faces: the decoded triangles after G3's degenerate-skip convention (F7). 0 for a vertices-only export (the G2 P7 pool-without-connectivity family, warning class no-facet-records).

min.description: Pool coordinate minimum per axis (x, y, z).

max.description: Pool coordinate maximum per axis (x, y, z).

bounding_box.description: The pool's coordinate extents (G2 P10: every pool-carrying part has a non-degenerate bbox).

class.description: Warning class. unresolved-facet-family: facet records of families whose primitive reading G3 has not pinned (0x41/0x44/0x49/0x4b/0x4e, open questions 3-5) and/or unparseable header candidates; where such records produce in-pool loops they still decode under the structural strip reading (G3's soup convention). degenerate-triangles-skipped: the G3 F7 skip convention fired (0 on every clean-store soup). open-shell: the mesh is a manifold with boundary edges (G3 F6's sheet-like open shells, legitimate geometry). unused-pool-vertices: pool positions no triangle references. no-facet-records: pool without any facet header candidate (G2 P7), exported vertices-only. curve-entry-loops-unexported: composite loops referencing skip slots (curve entries) — their coordinates live in the curve records (U4, open, stage-3d #34 2026-11-11) so those loops are not exported; the store's other loops export. curve-entry-loops-exported-dup-pin: the dup-pin weld (#34; stage-10 2026-11-12, per-loop decision from 2026-11-18) fired — each dropped curve-entry loop that is fully pinnable (every referenced skip slot has a preceding written element to weld to), battery-supported (its record carries no normal, or the dup-pinned coordinates are coplanar at 2e-3) and mesh-safe (its triangles keep the assembled mesh manifold, no degenerate emission) exported with each skip slot welded to that element's written vertex (no new vertices, the U4-D dup law); the decision is independent per loop and does not require an empty primary mesh; refused or unpinnable loops keep the conservative curve-entry-loops-unexported rule. duplicate-triangles-deduped: the stage-15 unordered-triangle dedup law (#34, 2026-11-13, the stage-14 review F1 family) fired — the emitted mesh was not-manifold and carried duplicate unordered index triples (the same facet re-written from a second record/loop, opposite winding, territory overlap 0), the deduplicated mesh is manifold, so the later copies dropped (first occurrence's winding kept; degenerate skips untouched). duplicate-triangles-dedup-declined: duplicates found but their removal leaves the mesh not-manifold — the dedup declined fail-closed and the emitted triangles are kept verbatim (0 measured corpus stores; the branch exists as the law's fail-closed arm). primary-loop-manifold-skip: the 2026-11-18 primary-emit seam guard skipped primary facet loops that would push an undirected edge past two uses and measure at most 0.1% of the mesh area assembled so far (slivers, not surface). primary-loop-manifold-kept: primary loops that over-use an edge were kept because each is larger than 1% of the assembled area — real surface is never dropped; the mesh stays not-manifold exactly as before and the over-use is named (owner decision, docs/evidence/2026-11-18-primary-emit-seam.md). primary-loop-manifold-declined: candidate sliver loops were found at the seam but the store stays not-manifold after they are out (a larger over-use is kept), so the seam is declined fail-closed and the pre-seam emission is returned unchanged. primary-loop-relist-skip: the Fase 3 L1 post-pass (issue #70, 2026-11-21) skipped kept primary facet loops whose triangles are the NX->CATIA writer's re-listed skin — removing them leaves the store mesh manifold with the boundary-edge set not growing (the detail carries the before->after boundary count); the skip is declined and the previous emission kept whenever either condition fails, and it runs only after the stage-15 dedup on the still-not-manifold residue. grid-candidates-refused: the grid fallback meshed at least one grid of the part but refused another (the detail carries the per-gate census); their bytes were not emitted. point-grid-meshed: the structured-point-grid fallback fired (2026-11-19, docs/evidence/2026-11-19-grid-meshing.md) — the mesh is an inferred candidate connectivity (two triangles per cell from the station order over row-major f64 point nets), not a decoded surface.

detail.description: Human-readable explanation citing the evidence claim.

warnings.description: Non-fatal decode observations, in a fixed order (degenerate-triangles-skipped, no-facet-records, open-shell, unused-pool-vertices, unresolved-facet-family). Empty on a fully clean decode.

store_ordinal.description: 0-based ordinal of the exported block among the blocks of the container family the store was located in (CATStdCont blocks for stores the shipped law located; the stage-3a probe family's blocks for recovered stores). With several blocks, the first store passing the export gate wins.

container.description: Container family whose region located the store (stage 3a #34; other-container added stage 12 #34 2026-11-13): stdcont = the shipped CATStdCont law, xdoclink = a CATXDocLinkCont region probe, seebody = a CATSeeBodyCont region probe (G1 N10's next_block_store family and the seebody stores, docs/evidence/2026-11-10-l2-grind-classification.md section 6), other-container = a store validated in a remaining block region of any other doc-type name (the stage-12 census: CATBRepModeContainer 39 / CameraStartupContainer 8 / contmeasure 2 / four others 1 each — docs/evidence/2026-11-13-noncomposite-census.md section 2).

tail_law.description: Catalog-tail law that validated the store (stage 3a #34): shipped = the pre-stage-3a window [cb, origin + dword8 + dword12); overshoot = the G1 C3 dword8-overshoot variant, read from the true catalog magic with length dword12; padded = the G1 padded-tail variant, ended at its CB__END (N4w).

container_name.description: The located block's own doc-type name (stage 12 #34, present only with container = other-container; e.g. CATBRepModeContainer).

store_recovery.description: Present only on recovered stores (stage 3a #34, the L5 lever; stage 12 #34 extends the probe families): how the store was located — which container probe and which catalog-tail law. Absent on stores located by the shipped CATStdCont law. A recovered store that then fails the decode names the same probe/law on the error detail instead.

origin_kind.description: G1's store-origin variant: v5header for the 32-byte V5_CFV2 header variant (N1h, 1,056/1,173), block for the header-less variant (N1l, origin = block start, 12 R19 parts).

pool_group_count.description: Number of decoded 01 06 pool groups in the store body (G2 P1g). The pool is flattened across groups in body order, G3's soup convention.

facet_candidate_count.description: Number of facet header candidates (the 01 [41-4f] . ff regex positions) in the store body.

facet_record_count.description: Number of facet records accepted by the (width, k) tiling law (G3 F1/F1w).

degenerate_triangle_count.description: Degenerate strip triangles skipped at decode (repeated vertex or zero cross product, G3 F7; 0 on every clean-store soup).

edge_count.description: Distinct undirected edges of the decoded triangles.

manifold.description: No edge used more than twice (G3 F6: 76/76 clean-store soups). Vacuously true at 0 faces.

closed.description: Every edge used exactly twice (G3 F6: 66/76 clean-store soups; false marks the sheet-like open shells, warning class open-shell). Vacuously true at 0 faces.

oriented.description: Each edge used once per direction (G3 F6: 66/66 of the closed soups; the winding law F5 preserved). Vacuously true at 0 faces.

boundary_edge_count.description: Edges used exactly once (0 on closed solids).

mesh.description: Mesh invariants over the decoded triangles (G3 soup_stats measures).

surface_tessellation.description: Additive exact-surface block (2026-11-19, docs/evidence/2026-11-19-surface-tessellation.md): present only when the exporter took the a5 03 34 B-spline fallback because the nested-store path produced no facet triangles. Carries the frame census (frames, decoded, evaluable, tessellated, refused, pole_points), the merged mesh's grid_points and the chord-error tolerance band (tolerance_fraction = 1e-3 of each pole-net bbox diagonal, tolerance_min/tolerance_max in mm). The warning class bspline-surface-tessellated marks the same route; open-shell is expected because each patch is an open sheet and patches are concatenated without topology joins.

grid_meshing.description: Additive structured-point-grid block (2026-11-19, docs/evidence/2026-11-19-grid-meshing.md): present only when the exporter took the point-grid fallback because the nested-store path produced no facet triangles AND the part carries no a5 03 34 frame. carriers = 3-divisible point runs considered; shaped = runs with a >=3x3 grid reading (the grid path's ownership gate); meshed = grids triangulated; refused + refusals name the failed gates (stalled stations/columns, degenerate cells, not-manifold, and the prefix dialect's non-monotone/non-uniform stations); duplicate_grids = identical point runs dropped; station_rows/columns = totals over the meshed grids; station_monotone = meshed grids whose station centroids are monotone; points = mesh vertices (one per grid point, no welding); connectivity = 'candidate' — the connectivity is an INFERENCE (two triangles per cell from the station order), never a decoded surface. The warning class point-grid-meshed marks the same route; open-shell is expected because every grid is an open sheet.

bagrep_face_gp.description: Additive face-gp block (#63, 2026-11-21, docs/evidence/2026-11-21-bagrep-face-gp.md): present only when the exporter took the CATSurfacicRep patch-stream fallback (after the facet stores, the a5 03 34 B-spline surfaces and the structured E5 grids, before the point-only display carriers). The records' 0x51 patch sub-records (30 04 04 ff ff ff d2 d2 51) decode under the CAT3DFaceGP law — kind 3 at +57, u16be indices after the ff 7f / 01 80 marker, v = idx // 3 into the record's declared f32 point array (one word after its count) — under the strict per-sub-record gate (byte-exact closure end == sub_len - 1, every index mult-3 and in-bounds, no repeated-index triangle, self-manifold) and the in-order assembly (unordered-triangle dedup first copy wins + the incremental mesh-safe guard). records = patch streams that emitted triangles (the records' declared arrays concatenated with disjoint index spaces); sub_records = every 0x51 sub-record in the CATSurfacicRep spans; sub_records_gated = strict-gate passes; guard_refused = assembly refusals; dedup_dropped = unordered duplicate triangles dropped. source = 'bagrep-face-gp'. The warning class bagrep-face-gp-meshed marks the same route; the mesh is manifold by construction (the gate + the guard) and the degenerate count stays 0 (the writer's zero-area slivers over duplicate pinned coordinates ride as decoded — the route's warning names it).

no_surface_display.description: Additive display-carrier block (2026-11-19, docs/evidence/2026-11-19-no-surface-fallback.md): present only when the part produced no facet triangles, no evaluable a5 03 34 surface and no triangulable point grid, yet carries decodable geometry. It is a faithful DISPLAY of the decoded carriers, never a surface reconstruction: surface = false, kind = decoded-carriers, label = the visible 'no surface — showing N points, M curve segments' text. points = a flat f32 xyz array of the decoded carrier points (the 3-divisible f64 point runs with their coordinates rounded once to f32, the store pool when the store path succeeded vertices-only, and the decoded 33 3X curve-record centers); curve_segments = a flat array of point-index pairs, emitted only where a curve law pins two endpoints (the 33 32 [P][Q][P]+|Q| reading's P -> P+Q; circles/conics expose no orientation, so they contribute a center point and never a guessed polyline). point_count / curve_segment_count count the arrays; regions, pool_points, point_runs, run_points, curve_records, decoded_curve_records, skipped_curve_records, curve_points, line_records and families carry the decode census, and grid_shaped/grid_refusals name the refused structured-grid candidates when the part had any. sources lists the non-empty carrier labels behind the points (decoded-carriers and/or bagrep-f32-points); bagrep_regions, bagrep_arrays, bagrep_floats, bagrep_points and bagrep_skipped carry the count-framed f32 array census from the geometry containers the missing-store census named (docs/evidence/2026-11-19-bagrep.md). Those arrays are coordinate write streams with no face list and no implicit strip, so they contribute points only — never a triangle, a weld or an inferred join. The warning class no-surface-display marks the same route; vertex_count and triangle_count stay 0 (the PLY is empty) and the §3.4 gate still records empty-mesh, so L2 is unchanged.

composite.description: Additive composite-only decode block (stage-2c/3d #34; present only on composite-space exports — consumers ignore unknown properties). Carries the identity decode counters (stage, element_decl, node_points, curve_entries, write_count, table_bytes, facet_candidates, facet_records, skipped_markers, loops_exported, loops_curve_entry) and, on multi-rep stores (stage identity-per-rep, the stage-4b per-rep law), reps_decoded / reps_exported / reps_unexported / rep_reasons. node_bytes (stage-5 fold-in, 2026-11-12, docs/agents/stage-3d-reconciliation.md section 5): the decoded list-node payload byte span(s) — the single list node's payload on single-rep stores (stage identity-table-walk), the sum of the scanned node payload spans on multi-rep stores; over 4096 B marks the big-form family, letting form be derived from summaries/CSVs. Stage-10 (2026-11-12, RELAXED stage-15 2026-11-13 — the E0-b battery criterion removed, owner-authorized): on a dup-pin firing store, curve_entry_law 'e0b-dup-pin' + loops_curve_entry_exported name the exported dup-pinned loops and loops_curve_entry counts only the loops still dropped (0 when the law exported them all). Stage-15 (2026-11-13): on a dedup firing store, unordered_dedup_dropped names the dropped duplicate copies; unordered_dedup_declined names a fired-and-declined dedup (duplicates found, removal leaves the mesh not-manifold, emitted triangles kept verbatim). Extended-header family (2026-11-18, docs/evidence/2026-11-18-extended-header-family.md): on stores carrying the 0x47/0x4f extended-header records, extended_header_records names the accepted record count and extended_header_triangles the triangles they emitted (single-rep and per-rep paths alike); extended_header_declined names the records the manifold-assembly gate declined — their triangles would have pushed an undirected edge past two uses in the assembled mesh, so they are not exported (the same incremental edge-use lever as the dup-pin weld) and the warning class extended-header-geometry-declined carries the count. Primary-emit seam (2026-11-18, docs/evidence/2026-11-18-primary-emit-seam.md): primary_loop_skips names the sliver loops dropped at the primary emission (each <= 1% of the store mesh’s area and over-using an edge), primary_loop_kept the larger over-using loops kept (real surface, mesh unchanged), and primary_loop_seam_declined the candidate slivers a still-not-manifold store returned unchanged (the fire gate).
